transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, we've got a 48-hour water conservation restriction from the municipal authority, and we need to reduce our normal process-water consumption during that period. I'll be making the final call on the water-control plan, but I want to hear from quality, maintenance, and EHS before I sign off. We've got 2,400 liters of reclaimed water available, and both Line X and Line Y are scheduled to run during the restriction. Let's start with updates — what does each of your areas need me to consider before I finalize the plan?

decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Reclaimed water will NOT be used for Line X due to conductivity exceeding the process limit. Reclaimed water will be used for Line Y only, after completing the 3-hour membrane flush, verifying sanitizer is adjusted to 0.3 ppm, signing the sanitizer log for each use day, and recording a conductivity test before use. Line X will use municipal process water under reduced consumption, and Line Y's 1,800-liter batch will be supplied from the 2,400 liters of reclaimed water available.

commitments.detail: Upload the reclaimed-water conductivity test result (1,800 microsiemens/cm) to the shared quality folder before any reclaimed water is used for Line Y.
Enter the recovery skid inspection findings into the work-order system and schedule the 3-hour membrane flush before reclaimed water delivery begins.
Attach the municipal permit review to the site's permit record, verify sanitizer is adjusted to 0.3 ppm, and ensure the sanitizer log is signed for each day of reclaimed water use.
Sign the water-control plan authorizing reclaimed water for Line Y only (1,800 liters) and municipal process water for Line X under reduced consumption for the 48-hour restriction period.
